headline: England's press finally breaks Congo's stubborn line
story: Congo DR stunned Atlanta Stadium with a seventh-minute goal that belied the evening's arithmetic. England pressed high from the start—9.2 sustained high-press phases to Congo's 1.1—and controlled territory with 53 per cent possession and 16 shots. Yet the pattern of the match was set early: one side bent and bent, the other broke through in flashes. England squandered chances at the thirty-fifth minute and in first-half injury time, the sort that separate draws from victories.

The turning point came at the forty-second minute when Congo DR had their clearest chance: a headed opportunity worth 0.57 expected goals that struck the post. England survived. What followed was patient, relentless pressure: a forty-three-second average ball recovery (to Congo's 22.5 seconds) and systematic exploitation of Congo's inability to hold shape. Kane and his midfield assembled two goals in the final quarter—one at seventy-five minutes, the decisive blow at eighty-six—both the product of wearing opponents down rather than brilliance.

keyMoment.text: Congo DR's header hits the post. That miss cost them everything.

home.verdict: Suffocating press and late precision prevailed, though early wastefulness almost cost them.
points: High press won the game: 9.2 phases forced Congo into reactive football throughout.
Ball recovery speed mattered: 13.8 seconds versus Congo's 22.5 gave England constant transitions.
Late execution: sixth goal (86') had only 0.06 xG, but it arrived on the back of total control.

away.verdict: One extraordinary miss at forty-two minutes decided the tie they might otherwise have stolen.
points: The post hurt them: 0.57 xG chance at forty-two; if scored, a very different second half beckons.
Pressing was absent: 1.1 phases against England's 9.2 meant they never contested the ball's ownership.
Recovery speed killed them: 22.5-second average left defenders perpetually scrambling after turnovers.

statLine: England's ball recovery of 13.8 seconds compared to Congo DR's 22.5 was the single metric that separated dominance from delusion: a ten-second chasm in transition speed.
